node-1.label: Intermittent, dull, throbbing, localized tenderness in an alopecic patch on the right parietal-occipital scalp for 2-3 months

node-2.label: Patient is a woman in her early twenties with a lifelong history of alopecia; the affected right parietal-occipital scalp alopecic patch has been stable in size and appearance since birth, and three other round alopecia patches present since birth remain asymptomatic

node-3.label: Clinical scalp examination revealed an atrophic white patch of alopecia, with ill-defined bogginess surrounding the lesion and extending to the central and posterior occipital scalp

attrs.why: Radiologist analysis explicitly supports a congenital scalp defect/aplasia cutis congenita, citing lifelong alopecic patches, atrophic bogginess, dermoscopy findings (translucent epidermis, branched vessels, marginal hair bulbs), and head CT without osseous/vascular/neural/soft-tissue defects; recent tenderness is atypical rather than infectious/neoplastic. Combined with the lifelong stable patches and atrophic boggy lesion, confidence increases from 0.75 to 0.80.

Radiologist analysis states the recent tenderness is not infectious, and dermoscopy/head CT show no signs of local infection or inflammation; the lifelong stable, asymptomatic alopecia also lacks acute inflammatory features. Confidence decreases from 0.10 to 0.05.
New dermoscopy and head CT findings show no neoplastic/adnexal features or soft-tissue mass; lifelong stability further refutes an aggressive neoplasm. Confidence decreases from 0.2 to 0.05.

New structural scalp findings (atrophic patch, dermoscopy abnormalities) support a congenital/atrophic anomaly rather than isolated primary neuralgia; the pain is better explained by the structural scalp defect. Confidence decreases from 0.1 to 0.05.

node-8.label: Dermoscopy shows translucent epidermis, branched vessels, and marginal hair bulbs

node-9.label: Head CT shows no osseous, vascular, neural, or soft-tissue defects

node-10.label: Aplasia cutis congenita of the scalp

attrs.why: Radiologist analysis specifically supports aplasia cutis congenita, noting dermoscopy with translucent epidermis, branched vessels, and marginal hair bulbs plus head CT without underlying defects; recent tenderness is atypical and not infectious/neoplastic. This raises confidence in the specific congenital scalp defect from 0.55 to 0.70, though birth records, scalp MRI/ultrasound, pathology, and genetics remain unavailable.
